claim: AREX Express from Incheon Airport to Seoul Station is non-stop, ~43 min from T1 (51 min from T2), costing about 11,000 KRW (cheaper online); the all-stop train runs every 5-10 min, takes ~59 min and costs up to ~5,350 KRW.
quote: Travel Time: 43 minutes (from T1) / 51 minutes (from T2)... The 2026 AREX Fare is 11,000 KRW for Express... all-stop fares are up to 5,350 KRW depending on destination

claim: A taxi from Incheon Airport to central Seoul takes 60-80 minutes and costs roughly 65,000-100,000 KRW including the ~7,900 KRW airport expressway toll, with international taxis about 20% more.
quote: estimated fare of 65,000–100,000 KRW (includes toll fees)... An additional toll for Incheon Int'l Airport Expressway (₩7,900)... International taxis are 20 percent more expensive

claim: Airport limousine/buses from Incheon to Seoul cost roughly 5,000-15,000 KRW and take about 60-80 minutes depending on traffic and destination.
quote: Tickets are KRW 5,000 to 15,000 and travel time is approximately 60 to 80 minutes, depending on traffic and destination

claim: Gimpo Airport (GMP) is inside the city, so AREX/subway reaches Seoul Station in ~20 min and Gangnam/COEX in ~38 min for ~1,550 KRW, far quicker than Incheon's 50km island location.
quote: Travel from Gimpo International Airport to Seoul Station takes about 20 minutes... Time: 25 mins to Yeouido... 38 mins to Gangnam/COEX... Price: ~1,550 KRW

claim: The Climate Card tourist pass costs 5,000 (1-day), 8,000 (2-day), 10,000 (3-day) and 15,000 (5-day) KRW for unlimited Seoul subway and city buses, but excludes bike-share and does not let you board AREX at the Incheon terminals (you can only alight there).
quote: 1-day Pass: KRW 5,000... 2-day Pass: KRW 8,000... 3-day Pass: KRW 10,000... 5-day Pass: KRW 15,000... you cannot take the train at T1 and T2

claim: The short-term Climate Card tourist pass requires no Korean phone number, ARC or online account, unlike resident monthly passes.
quote: The short-term Tourist Pass (1-7 days) does not require a Korean phone number, an Alien Registration Card (ARC), or any online account

claim: A reusable T-money card costs ~3,000-5,000 KRW at convenience stores and deducts ~1,550 KRW per subway ride; it works nationwide (Seoul, Busan, Jeju), making it better than the Seoul-only Climate Card for travel beyond the capital.
quote: You buy the physical card for roughly ₩3,000 to ₩5,000 at any convenience store. Every time you ride the subway, ₩1,550 gets deducted... a T-Money card works in Seoul, Busan, Jeju Island, and rural towns

claim: Citizens of 67 visa-waiver countries (incl. US, UK, EU, Canada, Australia, Japan) are temporarily exempt from K-ETA through December 31, 2026 and can enter visa-free for stays up to 90 days for tourism.
quote: extended the temporary exemption from the Korea Electronic Travel Authorization (K-ETA) requirement... until December 31, 2026... A visa is not required for stays 90 days or less for business or tourism

claim: K-ETA-exempt travelers must instead complete an e-Arrival Card (digital form) within 3 days before each arrival to Korea.
quote: An e-Arrival Card is a trip-specific digital form that must be completed within 3 days before every arrival and is mandatory for all travelers who do not have a K-ETA

claim: Google Maps gives unreliable walking/transit directions in Seoul due to Korea's map-data export restrictions, so Naver Map and KakaoMap (both with English support and real-time transit) are the reliable navigation apps; Google's high-precision data export was only conditionally approved in May 2026.
quote: South Korea has a unique law restricting the export of detailed mapping data... Google Maps' turn-by-turn navigation... is often wrong or missing entirely in Seoul... government conditionally approved Google's export of high-precision map data... as of May 2026

claim: Solo short-trip travelers are best served by an eSIM (instant QR activation, one-time cost), while groups or heavy/streaming users benefit from pocket WiFi with unlimited data; all three carriers (KT, SKT, LG U+) sell prepaid unlimited SIMs at Incheon Airport.
quote: all three major carriers (KT, SK Telecom, and LG U+) at Incheon Airport... offer prepaid SIMs with unlimited data... eSIM can be more cost-effective for travelers who plan to stay... for a shorter period

claim: Myeongdong is the most practical base for first-timers being central, walkable and well-connected, but is crowded and tourist-heavy; Insadong/Jongno offers traditional charm near the palaces; Hongdae is cheapest with the best nightlife and a direct AREX link; Gangnam is newer, larger-roomed and more upscale.
quote: Myeongdong is the most practical choice for first-timers, being central, walkable, well-connected by subway... Hongdae is the cheapest area... plus the most affordable accommodation and a direct AREX connection to Incheon Airport... Gangnam district's hotels are newer

claim: A standard 2-day Seoul skeleton spends Day 1 on traditional Seoul (Gyeongbokgung Palace with 10am guard change, walk to Bukchon Hanok Village, lunch in Insadong, Myeongdong night market from ~5pm) and Day 2 on modern Seoul (N Seoul Tower, cafes, K-beauty, shopping), leaving evening slots open.
quote: Start your day with a visit to Gyeongbokgung Palace... changing of the guard ceremony at 10 AM... walk to the nearby Bukchon Hanok Village... Head to Insadong... Visit the night market in Myeongdong... starting at around 5pm
